summary: Herman Sharp, writing on behalf of the Western Rockhound Association, argues that ORV damage is confined to relatively small, well-defined areas near urban centers, and that it is wasteful and unreasonable to evaluate and classify all 452 million acres of public domain land. He proposes that management agencies concentrate resources only in problem areas, identify those needing protection, and leave the rest of the public lands open to access. He supports some targeted regulation but strongly opposes broad restrictions that would prevent rockhounds and other outdoorsmen from accessing remote public lands via primitive roads.
